title: SQL injection authentication bypass
impact: The login form concatenates user input directly into the SQL query, so an attacker can supply an injection payload as the email and be authenticated as the administrator without knowing any password. This grants unauthorized access to admin-only features and any data or actions tied to that account.
remediation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) so input is treated as data, never as SQL code. Add server-side authentication checks that do not rely on string-built queries, and consider rate limiting on login attempts.

title: UNION-based SQL injection in product search
impact: The search endpoint pastes the q parameter into a SQL query, so an attacker can append a UNION SELECT and read data from other tables. In this case that exposes every user email address and password hash, enabling credential cracking, account takeover, and attacks against other systems where users reused passwords.
remediation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries. Run the application with a least-privilege database account, validate and whitelist search input, and suppress raw SQL error messages so attackers cannot map the schema.

title: XSS via reflected search input
impact: The search page passes the q parameter through Angular bypassSecurityTrustHtml and renders it as trusted HTML, so an attacker can craft a link containing script that executes in a victim browser. This allows session token theft, actions performed as the victim, or defacement of the page.
remediation: Remove the bypassSecurityTrustHtml call on user-controlled query parameters and let Angular escape the value by default. Add a Content Security Policy that blocks inline scripts and javascript: URLs, and validate or encode untrusted input before rendering.

title: Stored XSS in customer feedback
impact: The feedback comment is stored and later rendered as HTML in the administrator feedback table, so an attacker can persist a script that executes whenever an admin views the feedback. This enables session token theft and actions performed with administrator privileges.
remediation: Remove the innerHTML binding on stored feedback and let the framework escape the value by default, or apply a strict sanitizer before rendering. Add a Content Security Policy that blocks inline scripts and javascript: URLs.
